Blaise is right to hold local government in Alachua accountable.


Blaise Ingoglia (@GovGoneWild)

“Gut” the services? @AlachuaCounty wasted $83M of taxpayer dollars last year. 

Projections say Alachua would lose $56M with a $250K exemption. 

Even after an aggressive tax cut Alachua would STILL have more than enough to deliver services. 

Stop the scare tactics. Cut your budget.



— https://nitter.net/GovGoneWild/status/2061783215765864626#m

Info on property taxes revenue far outpacing population growth in Seminole County.


Abraham López (@AbeLopezFL)

77%.

That’s how much Seminole County’s property tax revenue grew in just six years. In Oviedo, it was 71%.

Our population grew about 4 to 5%.
Let that sink in. Government collected far more from us, to serve nearly the same number of people.

Every family in Florida knows what you do when costs rise faster than income: you tighten up and do more with less. Every nonprofit knows it

A trial court rejected a lawsuit against Florida’s new congressional redistricting map last week.

Today, the appeals court also ruled in Florida’s favor.  

Get ready for November!


Attorney General James Uthmeier (@AGJamesUthmeier)

Our team takes another win!

Florida's 1st District Court of Appeals just ruled against Marc Elias’ appeal and will not upend Florida’s new redistricting map.

Thanks to our attorneys for the outstanding work.



— https://nitter.net/AGJamesUthmeier/status/2061553

Brock dropping the hammer!


Brock Juarez (@Juarez_Brock)

Good news, Commissioner. I just did a very quick search and found a great place for you to start making cuts.

That Office of Equity & Inclusion is sitting on a $1.4 million budget this year, right?

gainesvillefl.gov/Government…





— https://nitter.net/Juarez_Brock/status/2061599018321391846#m

Property tax revenue for local govt in 2019 was $32 billion.

Today it is $60 billion.

The vast majority of property tax revenue is non-homestead residential and commercial.  

There have been local mileage increases but a lot of it is increased valuations.


Rick Shaftan -- Neighborhood Research and Media (@Shaftan)

What spending items have increased more than inflation and population?

Is this a statewide issue or limited to certain jurisdictions?

In a field overflowing with agenda-driven, factually-challenged “reporters,” she was conspicuous for her partisanship and aversion to the truth.

A reminder that Alfonsi was reporter on a 13-minute 60 Minutes feature this year that opened w a German police raid on a man’s apartment for posting a cartoon they didn’t like. Th

Nathan Reeder (@PropertyMan219)

Median FL home price is $400k, if 92% of your homes are assessed under $500k, that means they should be much higher.

Baseball’s Greatest Moments (@BBGreatMoments)

eddie mathews or chipper jones. who you starting a franchise with?





— https://nitter.net/BBGreatMoments/status/2061585797036302761#m

Blast from the past.  

When we dissolved the Disney-controlled local government Reedy Creek, legacy media (who had previously been harsh critics of Disney’s special deal) claimed it was going to lead to massive tax hikes.

Never happened.

Narrative pushers gonna narrative.


Eric Spencer (@JustEric)

Worth noting that the people claiming non-homestead taxes will rise are the same people who claimed that dissolving Reedy Creek would cause Orange County property tax to rise, and taxes actually w

92% of homesteads are assessed at $500k or less.


Leisa (@leisasalmons)

I appreciate the tax break but c’mon Ron, how many homesteaders have anything less than 1 million in real property in Florida?

I’m on 1 acre in Safety Harbor and you’re from Dunedin, is your property under 500k?



— https://nitter.net/leisasalmons/status/2061573598226043336#m

Florida’s Constitution prohibits an income tax.  

Moreover, property tax revenue is local, not state, and has nearly doubled in the past seven years.  

Exempting homestead properties from tax would return local property tax revenue to the levels of a few years ago.  

Taxing and spending less is a good thing.


Ken Girardin (@PolicyEngineer)

This will be how Florida ends up with a personal income tax.



— https://nitter.net/PolicyEngineer/status/2061544545523757432#m

Wow, partisans aren’t telling the truth?  Imagine that!


Scott Wagner (@ScottWagnerFL)

Anyone who’s (1) not separating homestead residential property tax from ALL property tax, (2) omitting the other streams of revenue to a county or (3) not giving context on what it took to provide annual services from 2019-25 in your county, is not giving you the entire picture.



— https://nitter.net/ScottWagnerFL/status/2061469670637457828#m

A lot of vested interests in continuing using the homes of Floridians as an ATM.


Jill (@JillG63)

Florida Association of county manager
Florida Association of county
Florida Association of counties trust

Florida local environmental resource agencies

As you should — congrats!


Daniel (@msgchief)

Your post is spot on Sir, we have owned are are new built starter home for 34 years and it has been homesteaded the whole time, I would pay zero property tax under the proposal but if would sell I would make a huge profit from sale price



— https://nitter.net/msgchief/status/2061563077611462856#m

Yeah this is a lie.  It fully eliminates property tax for 60% of homesteads and when raised to $500k exemption it will get 92% of homesteads fully exempt.

Median home value is not the same as the assessed value for tax purposes.

You can have a home valued at $250k for tax purposes that would sell for much more.


GUY (@guyferson)

While the idea and intention is correct — the median home value is around $375,000 in FL

Less than 25% of FL homes will qualify — half (or more) of the homes that q

Yes.


Just Jennifer (@JustJennifer369)

We bought a Florida home last March & are currently selling our home in Maine to then become Florida residents & homestead there. Will this apply to us as long as we become residents by the end of 2026?



— https://nitter.net/JustJennifer369/status/2061521434502107468#m

First, it requires the legislature to adopt a schedule to make homesteads fully exempt.  The $250k is the initial salvo.  

Second, 60% of the Legislature has to vote for it.  Many in the Legislature think the current proposal is too aggressive. Very few are saying it’s not aggressive enough.  That’s just the reality.


Mayor of DeSantisville (@DeSantisville)

I’d save 10% in phase 1 and 21% in phase 2. It last better than a poke in the eye but it’s a far cry from having them eliminated altogeth
